title: Composition of anchor-free run segments
statement: Let $c,d,e$ be configurations of the dual transducer on a fixed binary input, and let $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$. If running the transducer for $a$ steps from $c$ reaches $d$ without being in the anchor state at any time before step $a$, and running it for $b$ steps from $d$ reaches $e$ without being in the anchor state at any time before step $b$, then running it for $a+b$ steps from $c$ reaches $e$ without being in the anchor state at any time before step $a+b$.
hypotheses_covered: Configurations $c,d,e$ on a fixed binary input
The first run segment reaches $d$ in $a$ steps and avoids the anchor state at all earlier times
The second run segment reaches $e$ in $b$ steps and avoids the anchor state at all earlier times
replaced:
Let $c, d, e$ be configurations of the dual transducer. If running $a$ steps from $c$
reaches $d$ without visiting the anchor state before time $a$, and running $b$ steps
from $d$ reaches $e$ without visiting the anchor before time $b$, then running $a + b$
steps from $c$ reaches $e$ without visiting the anchor before time $a + b$.
